newsitem.title: USA: Dade County, Fla., economy strong in 1996--council.
newsitem.headline: Dade County, Fla., economy strong in 1996--council.

text.p: The economy in Florida's Dade County has seen strong growth for 1996, the Beacon Council business development group said in its quarterly economic report on Wednesday.
Total wage and salary employment rose to 950,000 at the quarter's end September 30, an increase of 13,400 jobs or 1.4 percent over last year.
Retail sales totalled $14.7 billion for the first eight months of 1996, an increase of 11.6 percent over last year.
The value of trade merchandise processed through the Miami Customs District rose to $18.7 billion in the first six months of the year, an increase of 6.1 percent over the same period last year.

The number of overnight visitors to Dade County rose to 4.9 million for the first six months of the year, up 4.2 percent over the same period last year. Visitor spending was $5.5 billion for the period, an increase of 46 percent over the first six months of 1995.
On the downside, permit valuations fell by 35 percent for residential construction and by 11 percent for non-residential construction during the first eight months of the year, the council said.
The forecast for 1997 calls for continued economic growth, but at slower rates, the council said.
Dade County encompasses the Miami urban area.
